Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. It appears as small, black spots on older leaves, which develop concentric rings (target-like pattern).
Potato___Early_blight.advice: Apply fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Rotate crops and remove infected plant debris after harvest to reduce fungal spores.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is a serious disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. It shows as large, irregular water-soaked spots that rapidly turn brown or black, often with white mold on the underside.
Potato___Late_blight.advice: Immediate application of copper-based fungicides is needed. Improve air circulation and avoid overhead watering. If severe, remove and destroy infected plants immediately.

Potato___healthy.description: The leaf appears healthy with no visible signs of fungal or bacterial infection. It shows good color and turgor.
Potato___healthy.advice: Continue regular monitoring. Maintain proper watering and nutrition schedules to keep the plant resilient against future diseases.
